newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FORECAST - Property, telecom to boost Metro.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Property, telecom to boost Metro.

text.p: Property sales and an expanding cellular phone subscriber base would boost the bottom line of diversified conglomerate Metro Pacific Corp in 1996 and 1997, a Reuters poll showed.
The survey of five brokerage houses completed on Tuesday yielded an average 1996 net profit forecast of 704 million pesos, up 37 percent from 513 million in the previous year.
The firm's 1997 net profit was expected to rise further to 1.1 billion pesos.
Turnover would range from 5.180 billion pesos to 6.450 billion pesos for 1996, and 7.620 billion pesos to 8.025 billion pesos for this year, the analysts said.
Metro Pacific, the Philippine flagship of Hong Kong's First Pacific Co Ltd, was seen benefiting the most from its telecommunications and real estate units.

Smart Communications Inc, a joint venture with its parent First Pacific and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Inc, is the second biggest cellular phone provider in the country. It had a subscriber base of 275,000 as of last November.

Metro's real estate venture is Bonifacio Land Corp in which its owns a 40 percent stake. This firm in partnership with the government is developing a new business district in fort Bonifacio, formerly an army cantonment in Manila.

"Metro is anticipated to reap more fruits from its massive investment programme during the past three years as Smart and FBDC spearhead a 143 percent bottomline increment to 1.16 billion pesos," Tonette Singson, an analyst of Pryce Securities, said.
FBDC is Fort Bonifacio Development Corp in which stakeholders are the government and Bonifacio Land Corp.
"Income from its telecommunications and property development units are anticipated to be the main drivers of growth over the medium term," Singson said in a report.
"We estimate that the net profit of FBDC will show a compounded growth rate of around 113 percent over the period 1996 to 1999," David George of DBP-Daiwa Securities said.
Regina Manzano, investment analyst of Philipine Asia Equity Inc, said the start of the sale of its Pacific Plaza Tower in Fort Bonifacio should boost its bottomline.
"We are looking at a strong growth in the Bonifacio project," she said.
But the good news from Fort Bonifacio and Smart Communications would be slightly offset by the poor performance of its corrugated box making unit Steniel Manufacturing Corp, the analysts said.
Steniel reported a net loss of 127.2 million pesos in the first nine months of 1996, mainly because of higher raw materials costs.
Steniel was expected to return to better times in the next few years as it has begun streamlining its operations.
The company is disposing one of its plants in Manila.

Its banking unit PDCP Development Bank and consumer products subsidiaries Metrolab, Metro Bottled Water Corp, Holland Pacific Paper Inc, and Philippine Cocoa Corp are expected to show average performances.
"These subsidiaries are not leaders in their area, but they turn in decent profits," Asia Equity's Manzano said.
